Sparse Poisson log-concave nonnegative matrix factorization

Source: R/spoloconmf.R
spoloconmf.Rd

Recover compounds with nonnegative spectra and log-concave elution profiles from a matrix of Poisson observations. A sparse deconvolution fit supplies candidate profiles; spectral clustering, local fusion and Poisson updates recover broader or asymmetric compounds while retaining every outcome channel.

Usage

spoloconmf(
  X,
  y,
  background = NULL,
  lambda = "gic",
  ncores = NULL,
  control = list(),
  verbose = FALSE
)

# S3 method for class 'spoloconmf'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'spoloconmf'
fitted(object, ...)

Arguments

X

Nonnegative design matrix whose columns are contiguous, log-concave candidate profiles, for example shifted copies of a point-spread function from convmatrix. Dense and sparse matrices are supported. Columns are normalized to unit sum internally.

y

Nonnegative count matrix, with scans in rows and outcome channels in columns, or a count vector for a single channel.

background

Optional nonnegative background basis with nrow(y) rows, for example a low-df B-spline basis. Its coefficients are nonnegative and unpenalized. NULL fits without a background.

lambda

Information-criterion preset ("gic", "bic", "aic", "ebic" or "mbic"), or a finite nonnegative numeric compound penalty. See Details for its scale.

ncores

Number of OpenMP threads. NULL uses the physical cores available on the machine.

control

Named list of optional controls: broad_repeats = 2L, full_sweeps = 1L, final_polishes = 2L, native_sweeps = 8L, block_sweeps = 12L, and psf_width = NULL. The last is the typical PSF full width at half maximum in scans; by default it is inferred from the middle design column.

verbose

Print the time, objective change and compound count at each stage.

x, object

A fitted spoloconmf object.

...

Additional arguments to S3 methods.

Value

An object of class "spoloconmf" containing sparse profiles H, spectra S, background coefficients alpha, fitted means mu, the background basis, the objective and stage ledger history, timing information seconds, and resolved controls. fitted() returns the fitted mean matrix.

Details

The mean is \(\mu = HS + B A\), where each column of \(H\) is a unit-sum elution profile, rows of \(S\) are spectra and \(BA\) is the smooth background. Profiles have contiguous support and satisfy \(\Delta^2 \log H_{\cdot k} \leq 0\) on their positive support.

The selection objective is \(-2\ell(y;\mu) + \lambda_R K\), with \(K\) the number of compounds. An IC preset sets \(\lambda_R = m\lambda_{IC}\), where \(m\) is the number of outcome channels. A numeric lambda specifies \(\lambda_R\) directly; the initial grouped deconvolution then uses \(\lambda_R/m\). This compound-count criterion assigns one count per compound. Spectral entries and profile complexity have no additional penalty.

Clustering proposes fusions from normalized spectra and overlapping profiles without fitting a model. Proposals are subsequently checked with local Poisson updates, holding the rest of the fitted signal in an offset. Every completed stage is accepted only when the objective on all original observations improves. The stage ledger records rejected proposals too. Sparse profiles remain sparse in the native spectral updates, which run across channels using OpenMP.

See also

L0glm_sparse_deco, L0glm_blind_deco, L0glm.fit

Examples

set.seed(12)
n <- 300L
psf <- convkernel("gaussian", 21L, list(sigma = 2))
X <- convmatrix(psf, n)
H <- cbind(X[, c(45, 95, 160, 235)],
           pmax(0, 1 - abs(seq_len(n) - 185) / 22))
H <- H %*% Matrix::Diagonal(x = 1 / Matrix::colSums(H))
S <- matrix(rexp(5 * 8, rate = 1 / 3000), 5, 8)
B <- splines::bs(seq_len(n), df = 4, intercept = TRUE)
mu <- as.matrix(H %*% S) + B %*% matrix(20, 4, 8)
Y <- matrix(rpois(length(mu), mu), n, 8)
fit <- spoloconmf(X, Y, background = B, ncores = 2L)
fit
matplot(fit$H, type = "l", lty = 1, xlab = "Scan", ylab = "Elution profile")
